title: Erb Street corridor community planning permit system approved
subtitle: 2025 surplus allocation, school-zone speed calming, Laurel Creek pumping station tender, and a development charge deferral for rental housing.
overview: Council approved a Community Planning Permit System for the Erb Street corridor {{vote:m11}}. It combines zoning changes, minor variances and site plan approval into one application with a 45-day decision window. Staff said existing height and density permissions carry over, and that fees mirror current ones. A development industry delegate raised concerns about fees, exemptions and costs during the water-capacity development freeze.

Council also allocated the 2025 property-tax base surplus of $1,259,811. It went to the Winter Control Reserve, a new Arts and Creative Industries Reserve and the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve {{vote:m7}}. Council moved $229,000 of capital funding to school-zone automated speed enforcement retrofits {{vote:m8}}.

Council awarded the Laurel Creek Sanitary Pumping Station tender for a total of $10,289,314.85 {{vote:m9}}. It approved a development charge deferral framework to support 553 rental units at 85 Bridgeport Road East {{vote:m10}}. Council met in closed session earlier in the day, and the minutes report no public decisions from it.

decisions.item: Erb Street Community Planning Permit By-law
decisions.detail: Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-26-06 and the Community Planning Permit By-law for the Erb Street Corridor, with related amendments and a new Complete Community Contribution Reserve Fund to be set up {{vote:m11}}.
Council allocated the $1,259,811 surplus: $650,000 to Winter Control, $250,000 to a new Arts and Creative Industries Reserve, and $359,811 to Tax Rate Stabilization.

decisions.item: Automated speed enforcement and traffic calming
decisions.detail: Council released $229,000 from the Transportation Master Plan Implementation and Sign Replacement project and reallocated it to the Automated Speed Enforcement School Zone Retrofit Project.

decisions.item: Laurel Creek Sanitary Pumping Station tender
decisions.detail: Council awarded RFT26-01 to Finnbilt General Contracting Limited for $10,289,314.85 including unrecoverable HST, and approved up to $1,300,000 in Development Charges debenture financing for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive project.

decisions.item: Development charge deferral for 85 Bridgeport Road East
decisions.detail: Council approved a Development Charges Act section 27 deferral framework for a development of 553 rental units, and authorized the City Treasurer to sign the agreement subject to Regional approval.
Council approved revised Terms of Reference for the Municipal Election Compliance Audit Committee.

debate: A delegate from the development industry supported streamlined approvals but said the new system adds cost and process while water capacity limits building permits. The delegate asked for lower or deferred fees, broader exemptions, including for 10 units or fewer, and deferral of the 4% community contribution.

Staff said the 4% Complete Community Contribution matches the community benefits charge paid today, and that Class 1 to 3 fees follow existing minor variance, site plan and rezoning fees. Applicants, not taxpayers, should cover review costs.

Staff explained that developments of four units and four storeys are exempt, matching a recent council decision. Staff did not exempt five to 10 units because of site design issues such as snow clearing, loading, parking and lighting, though the planning director can exempt some. Applications already in the pipeline are covered by transition and exemption provisions.

One councillor, who voted against, said it was contradictory to cite market hardship to defer affordable housing requirements but not the 4% fee, and suggested temporary incentives to get building permits moving.

On speed enforcement, one councillor asked about speed bumps on a major collector road and school-zone bus access. Staff said vertical deflection is limited to school zones, with designs suited to buses and snow plows, and that provincial funding must be spent by March 31, 2028.
